title: Dynamic Role Coverage Matrix & Tranche-Swap Protocol for Midcycle Interruptions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We often see sudden midcycle interruptions (urgent incidents, unexpected hiring gaps, or priority pivots) that force last-minute swaps across tranches. Current guidance focuses on scope cuts and surge lanes but lacks a compact, action-first protocol for swapping people while preserving critical skills and minimizing rework. This ticket delivers a practical Role Coverage Matrix and a Tranche-Swap Protocol: a lightweight playbook for PMs/Eng managers to execute safe temporary reassignments with measurable SLAs and rollback criteria.

Goals:
1) Create a Role Coverage Matrix template that maps critical skills to primary/secondary owners, cross-training level, and warm-pairing notes.
2) Define a fast Tranche-Swap Protocol (TSP) with decision gates, communication steps, and timeboxed handover checklists (15/48/120 hour variants).
3) Add tooling hints for automating matrix lookups (Confluence template + a simple Google Sheet with filters) and integrate swap logs into the cycle dashboard for auditability.
4) Reduce time-to-stabilize after an interruption by 30% in pilot teams, and enable safe swaps without increasing regression risk.

Out-of-scope: Full capacity-simulation engine, large-scale headcount reallocation policy, and C-level approvals for permanent role changes (this is focused on temporary midcycle swaps).

Proposed deliverables:
- Role Coverage Matrix template (Confluence + downloadable CSV) with fields: Role, Primary owner, Secondary owner, Cross-train level (0-3), On-call familiarity, Handoff checklist link, Key repositories, Test harnesses impacted, Expected warm-up hours.
- Tranche-Swap Protocol doc with three execution tiers (15h emergency, 48h short swap, 120h planned swap), including acceptance tests, rollback triggers, and sign-off checklist.
- Quick-play swap checklist for daily standups and on-call rotations.
- Pilot runbook for two product teams (Console UX and Dedicated infra) with before/after metrics and play-by-play notes.
- Dashboard tile spec: swap events, warmup hours logged, post-swap regression count, and time-to-first-meaningful-commit.

Acceptance criteria:
- Confluence Role Coverage Matrix template created and approved by at least two Eng managers and one Design lead.
- Tranche-Swap Protocol reviewed and signed-off by PM leads and two Eng leads; includes explicit rollback criteria and a communication template for Slack and status pages.
- Pilot executed for one mid-size cycle (minimum 1 swap per pilot team) with metric collection and a short learnings doc.
- Dashboard tile prototype available as a lightweight CSV import and documented for Console team.

Tasks (high level):
- Draft matrix template + example populated for Console team (owner: Liam)
- Draft protocol with 15/48/120 hour variants (owner: Aisha)
- Instrument swap log CSV + dashboard tile spec (owner: Analytics: Priya Rao)
- Run pilot and collect metrics (owner: PM partner: Diego Alvarez)
- Post-pilot retro and iterate on template (owner: Aisha)

Trade-offs and notes:
- Keeping the matrix simple trades off granularity for speed; prefer rapid decisions over exhaustive skill scoring.
- Protocol tiers avoid micromanagement: the 15h path must favor immediate containment and re-routing rather than full handover.
- We will not attempt to automate assignment decisions in v1 — human PM/EM judgement remains primary.

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/confluence/display/PM/Role+Coverage+Matrix+Draft
- Example populated matrix (Console): https://drive.google.com/console-role-matrix-example
- Swap log CSV template: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/swap-log-template
- Related incident learnings: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234INCIDENT/p1670001234567

Monitoring & metrics:
- Time-to-stabilize (hours) pre/post pilot
- Number of post-swap regressions 
- Warmup hours logged per swapped engineer
- Qualitative feedback from affected engineers and PMs

Risks:
- Over-burdening secondaries if too many swaps occur concurrently (mitigate with swap caps per week).
- Insufficient telemetry to detect regressions immediately (mitigate with short post-swap smoke tests).

Next steps:
- Review draft with two Eng managers (target 2026-03-06)
- Populate Console example (target 2026-03-10)
- Begin pilot (target 2026-03-15)
